summary: Shoko Takeuchi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University. He later served as an emeritus professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1987–1995).

Shoko Watanabe was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji and Ernst Leumann, and later held professorships at Taisho University (1935–1943) and Toyo University (1956–1969).

Shoku Bando is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Kyoto University of Education, Otani University, and the University of Freiburg, and in 1987 held positions at the Abhidharma Institute, Kyoto University, and Fukui Prefectural College.

Shoryu Katsura specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He studied at Kyoto University and the University of Toronto, under scholars including Anthony Kennedy Warder, and served as professor at Hiroshima University (1976–2004) and Ryukoku University (2004–2015).

Shoshin Fukihara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University under Susumu Yamaguchi and at Horyuji Kangakuin under Join Saeki. He held posts at Otani University, Otani Senshu Gakuin, Doho University, and Otani University Junior College.

Shoshin Ichishima is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as Dean of Academic Affairs (attested 1983) and Professor Emeritus (attested 2014) at Taisho University, and as a visiting lecturer at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.

Shoshin Kuwayama is a scholar of history, archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Kyoto University (~1958–1966), he served there as assistant professor (~1973–1989) and Institute for Research in the Humanities professor emeritus (~1966–2002).

Shoshun Hayashidera is a scholar in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Affiliations include the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2011) and a professorship at Hokkaido University (attested 2026).

Shoson Miyamoto was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Otani University, the University of Tokyo, and the University of Oxford. His main posts included professorships at the University of Tokyo, Toyo University (~1928–1943), and Komazawa University (~1958–1974).
Shou-chien Shih is a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. He served as a professor at National Taiwan University (~1987–2003) and as director of the National Palace Museum (~2000–2004).

Shozen Kumoi was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at Otani University and under Erich Frauwallner at the University of Vienna. He held posts at Otani University (1948–1981) and Bukkyo University (1982).
Shri Krishna Saksena was a scholar of philosophy and Indology. He held professorships at the University of Lucknow and the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa.
Shri Krishna Sharma was an Indology and linguistics scholar. He founded the Hindu Maha Sabha and DAV College, Suva, and taught Dieter Schuh.

Shridhar Ramakrishna Bhandarkar was an Indologist. He served at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (1884), and held posts as Professor of Sanskrit at Elphinstone College and Wilson College, Mumbai.
Shridhar Tryambak Pathak was an Indologist. He was a Shastri at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute (attested 1921) and a Sanskrit Teacher at Elphinstone College (attested 1927).

Shrikant S. Bahulkar is a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Vasudev Vishnu Gokhale. He served as a professor at Tilak Maharashtra Vidyapeeth (1981–2009) and as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

Sri Narayana Mishra is a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and philosophy who studied under Anantalal Thakur. He spent his career at Banaras Hindu University as Lecturer, Reader, and Professor Emeritus of Sanskrit (attested 1971–2010).

Shripad Krishna Belvalkar was an Indologist and philosopher who studied under Kashinath Bapu Pathak and Charles Rockwell Lanman. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Deccan College (~1907–1927) and General Editor of the Mahabharata at BORI (1948–1961).

Shrivatsa Goswami is an Indology, religious studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at Banaras Hindu University. He taught philosophy and religion at Banaras Hindu University and was a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Shu-chen Chen is a scholar in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She completed a PhD at the University of Virginia, studying under supervisors Jeffrey Hopkins and Karen Christina Lang, and worked there as a teaching assistant in 1996.
